extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and journalists/editors covering wartime events
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and publishing newspaper accounts of wartime events, including use of official communiqués, eyewitness testimony, and navigating censorship and public-safety advisories. Emphasis on attribution, labeling source reliability, and limiting sensitive material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Censorship request: limit reporting on sensitive diplomatic disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: British censor requested English and foreign-language newspapers refrain from printing anything on the Polish-Soviet boundary dispute 'except official utterances.' The ban extends to news dispatches sent abroad and is more rigid than that on the domestic press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a topic might prejudice negotiations between governments, print only official utterances; avoid independent or speculative coverage that could aggravate diplomatic matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit publication of material prejudicial to allied relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Censorship was imposed 'to prevent publication abroad of matter considered prejudicial to relations between any of the United Nations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should withhold or limit reporting of items judged likely to harm relations between allied states; prioritize official statements and coordinated messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source attribution: name the source of information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Evening Standard and Daily Telegraph carried stories 'without giving the source of their information,' a practice noted in the dispatches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide named sources or clearly indicate the origin of reports; lack of source attribution undermines credibility and should be avoided where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label source reliability and type (official, unofficial, recorded)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports consistently identify origin — e.g., 'in a communique, broadcast by the Berlin radio and recorded by the Associated Press,' 'unofficial naval sources said,' 'the Moscow radio in a broadcast recorded by Reuter.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly tag information with source type (official communique, broadcast, unofficial source) so readers can gauge reliability; use qualifiers like 'official', 'unofficial', 'reported', 'recorded by...' as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on recorded broadcasts and official communiqués for factual claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Dispatches base factual claims on official communiqués and recorded radio broadcasts (e.g., German High Command communique recorded by Associated Press; Allied communiqués from headquarters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting operational details or casualty figures in wartime, cite official communiqués or recorded broadcasts as primary evidence; indicate when figures are claimed by an official source rather than independently verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use eyewitness and survivor testimony to convey human impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories include vivid survivor accounts and quotations (for example, witnesses describing crushed and suffocated babies, families wiped out, and survivors' descriptions of bodies on stairs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include first-hand testimony to humanize and illustrate events, but attribute personal accounts clearly and be mindful of graphic details and their potential effect on audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue public-safety advisories from authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ministry of Home Security warned Britons about a new small anti-personnel bomb—describing size, weight and hazard—informing the public what to watch for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When authorities issue safety warnings (e.g., new weapons, public hazards), report the advisory verbatim with practical details (appearance, risks) so the public can take precautions; attribute the source of the advisory.
